title: The derived adjunction $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be as in [def-sfb-finite-derived-pullback-iso] and $g\colon Z\to Y$ a
morphism. The adjunction $g^*\dashv g_*$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction]
induces an adjunction

$$
Lg^*\dashv Rg_*
$$

between the total derived functors on the unbounded derived categories
[sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]: $Lg^*$ computed on K-flat resolutions of
$D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$, $Rg_*$ on K-injective resolutions of
$D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ and $\mathcal D=\Sh(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$. Use the small skeletons and common larger universe of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; only its site and size convention are used, not its specialization to ring-module coefficients. The coefficient category has exactly the closed symmetric monoidal, Grothendieck abelian and additive-tensor hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed]. Clause (1) of that node makes both $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ Grothendieck abelian. Hence [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] gives K-injective resolutions of every unbounded complex in either category.

source.place: Proof: general derived adjunction, specialized to the exact pullback

proof.text: Write $F=g^*:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $G=g_*:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. Their adjunction, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, is [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction], and $F$ is exact by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact]. Both functors are additive: $F$ is exact; $G$, being a right adjoint, preserves zero objects and binary products by the adjunction's Hom bijections. In an additive category these are biproducts. Under the resulting product identification, $G$ preserves projections and zero maps, hence also injections (characterized by their composites with the projections), diagonals and codiagonals. The formula $a+b=\nabla\circ(a\oplus b)\circ\Delta$ proves additivity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] to get a natural bijection $\Hom_{K(\mathcal D)}(FM,I)\cong\Hom_{K(\mathcal C)}(M,GI)$, with forward map $[f]\mapsto[G(f)\circ\eta_M]$ and inverse $[a]\mapsto[\varepsilon_I\circ F(a)]$.

source.place: Proof: general derived adjunction, specialized to the exact pullback

proof.text: Let $Q_{\mathcal C},Q_{\mathcal D}$ denote localization to the unbounded derived categories. By [def-sfb-finite-derived-pullback-iso] the K-flat total left derived functor in the statement has a natural isomorphism $c:LF\xrightarrow{\sim}D(F)$, where $D(F)(Q_{\mathcal C}M)=Q_{\mathcal D}(FM)$. In particular this step uses the existence and comparison asserted by that node, rather than assuming that a K-flat complex is K-projective. The Right derived functors clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], applied to the additive $G$ and the K-injective resolutions in step 1, constructs $RG$ and computes $RG(Q_{\mathcal D}N)$ by $Q_{\mathcal C}(GI)$ for a K-injective resolution $N\to I$. These are precisely the two total derived functors required in the statement.

source.place: Proof: general derived adjunction, specialized to the exact pullback

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with its $\mathcal A=\mathcal D$, $\mathcal B=\mathcal C$, $u=G$ and $v=F$. The adjunction, additivity and exactness required there were checked in step 2. Consequently $GI$ is K-injective whenever $I$ is K-injective. Thus $I$ represents $L$ on $Z$, and $GI$ represents $RG L$ on $Y$, both by K-injective complexes.

For $K=Q_{\mathcal C}M$ and $L=Q_{\mathcal D}N$, choose a K-injective resolution $N\to I$. The comparison $c$ of step 3 and localization of this resolution identify the following groups:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\Hom_{D(\mathcal D)}(LFK,L)
&\cong\Hom_{D(\mathcal D)}(Q_{\mathcal D}FM,Q_{\mathcal D}I)\\
&\cong\Hom_{K(\mathcal D)}(FM,I)\\
&\cong\Hom_{K(\mathcal C)}(M,GI)\\
&\cong\Hom_{D(\mathcal C)}(K,RG L).
\end{aligned}
$$
The second and fourth bijections are [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], applied to $I$ and to $GI$ from step 4; the middle bijection is [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Here the first bijection sends $h:LFK\to L$ to $Q(N\to I)\circ h\circ c_K^{-1}$. Naturality for complexes follows from naturality of the localization maps and the termwise adjunction. It extends to all derived morphisms in $K$: $D(F)$ sends inverted quasi-isomorphisms to isomorphisms, and an equality expressing naturality for an invertible arrow also expresses naturality for its inverse. For the second variable, a derived map between K-injective representatives has a unique homotopy class representative by the same Hom-computation lemma; applying $G$ to it is the resolution computation of $RG$ and respects the middle bijection. Any two K-injective representatives of $L$ are connected by the unique homotopy class representing the identity of $L$; this is a homotopy equivalence, again by that lemma. The displayed bijection is therefore independent of the representative and natural in both derived variables. Denote it by $\Phi_{K,L}$.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, and Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives: the Hom adjunction used in its proof; comparison with the blueprint proof

proof.text: Define the derived unit by $\eta^d_K=\Phi_{K,LFK}(\mathrm{id}_{LFK})$ and the derived counit by $\varepsilon^d_L=\Phi^{-1}_{RG L,L}(\mathrm{id}_{RG L})$. Naturality gives $\Phi(h)=RG(h)\circ\eta^d_K$ and $\Phi^{-1}(a)=\varepsilon^d_L\circ LF(a)$. Substituting $h=\varepsilon^d_L$ gives $RG(\varepsilon^d_L)\circ\eta^d_{RG L}=\mathrm{id}_{RG L}$; substituting $a=\eta^d_K$ gives $\varepsilon^d_{LFK}\circ LF(\eta^d_K)=\mathrm{id}_{LFK}$. These are the two triangle identities, so the data define $LF\dashv RG$. They are induced by the original adjunction: on a K-flat representative $P$ and a K-injective resolution $FP\to I$, the unit is represented by $P\xrightarrow{\eta_P}GFP\to GI$; on a K-injective $I$ and a K-flat resolution $S\to GI$, the counit is represented by $FS\to FGI\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_I}I$. These follow directly from the two middle formulas in step 2 and the comparisons in step 3. Define the adjunction of the item to be this construction; its functors retain the K-flat and K-injective computations specified in the statement.
